learning_outcomes.text: The course aims to enable students to elaborate acquired concepts in order to be able to use them to interpret and describe some problems of applied sciences and in particular engineering.
Provide the foundations of mathematical language and an adequate mastery of the fundamental concepts of linear algebra and Cartesian geometry.

syllabus_topics: Infinitesimal calculus for curves and functions of several variables
Integral calculus for functions of several variables and vector functions
Series of Functions
Infinitesimal calculus for curves: vector-valued functions, limits and continuity; regular curves and vector differential calculus; arc length; line integrals of the first kind.

Differential calculus for real functions of several variables: graphs and level sets; limits and continuity for functions of several variables; topology in Rn and properties of continuous functions; partial derivatives, tangent plane, differential; higher-order derivatives, second differential, Hessian matrix; optimization; free extrema.
Integral calculus for functions of several variables: double integrals, reduction method, change of variables, calculation of volumes.
Vector fields: vector fields and line integrals of the second kind; Gauss-Green formula in the plane.

Series of functions: total convergence, theorems of continuity of the sum, term-by-term differentiability and integration by series. Power series and Taylor series; trigonometric series and introduction to Fourier series.
Complex numbers.
Vector spaces.
Bases and dimension.
Linear applications and isomorphisms.
Matrices.
Determinants.
Linear systems.
Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors.
Diagonalization.
Geometric vectors.
Affine space and parallelism.
Euclidean space and orthogonality.
Projective space.
Conics.
Quadrics (brief mention).

Elements of logic. Negation of a proposition. Proof techniques. Principle of induction. Applications. Composition. Invertibility. Relations and Partitions. Operations. Algebraic structures. Residue classes modulo n. The field Z_p.
The field of complex numbers C. Immersion of the real field in C. The imaginary unit. Trigonometric representation: modulus and argument. N-th roots of a complex number.
Vector spaces. Vector spaces of functions. Generating systems. Linear dependence. Bases and coordinates of a vector. Dimension.
Linear applications. The space Hom(V,W). Linear applications defined on the vectors of a base.
Kernel and image of a linear application. Isomorphic vector spaces and their dimension.
Vector spaces of matrices. Row-column product. Matrix of a linear application. Matrix of a composite linear application. Matrix of a change of base.
Calculation of the determinant of a matrix. Determinant of the transpose and determinant of a product. Invertibility of a matrix, its determinant, linear dependence of columns.
Cramer's systems. Rank of a matrix. Homogeneous linear systems and solution space.
Non-homogeneous linear systems and Rouché-Capelli theorem. Associated homogeneous system. Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors. Diagonalization.
Lines and oriented segments. Affine and Cartesian references. The space of geometric vectors. Coordinates of a vector and the endpoints of its representatives.
Parallelism and coplanarity between vectors and conditions on their coordinates.
Alignment and coplanarity conditions between points. Parametric representation of lines and planes. Cartesian equation of a plane and attitude parameters.
Bundles of planes and lines. Cartesian equations of a line and direction parameters. Parallelism conditions. Changes of affine reference.
Euclidean Space.
Definitions of angles. Scalar product. Distance between two points, sphere. Unit vector of an oriented line and direction cosines. Orthogonality conditions.
Projective extension of affine space. Representation of lines and planes in homogeneous coordinates.
Complexification of the real plane. Isotropic lines and cyclic points. Algebraic curves (brief mention). Bézout's theorem.
Classification of conics. Conic through five points. Bundles of conics. Configuration of base points and degenerate conics of a bundle.
Quadrics (brief mention).
assessment_rules: The final grade for the Mathematics II exam will be the average of the grades from the two modules (Analysis and Geometry). It is mandatory to have taken the Mathematics I exam. The written exam for Analysis lasts 3 hours and involves solving three exercises. The oral exam for Analysis lasts approximately 40 minutes. The Geometry module assessment includes a written test to assess mastery of linear algebra tools and their application, and an oral test to verify theoretical knowledge and comprehension.
